name: @tasklite/mcp

tools.name: connection_status
tools.description: Check whether this machine is connected to a TaskLite account. Call this first if any tool fails with an auth error.

tools.name: sign_up
tools.description: Create a brand-new TaskLite account + organization and connect this machine, no website visit needed. A strong random password is generated locally and never shown or stored; for web access the user later uses "forgot password" with this email. Ask the user for email, their name, and a business name before calling.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Connect this machine to an existing TaskLite account, or switch to a different one. Takes a personal API key (tl_...) created at TaskLite → Integrations → "Connect Claude Code". Replaces the current connection if there is one, use this to switch user or organization. The switch takes effect immediately; no restart.

apiKey.description: Personal TaskLite API key, starts with tl_

tools.name: login
tools.description: Connect this machine to an existing TaskLite account with email + password, or switch to a different account. Creates a personal API key named "claude-code" on that account and stores it, so the password is used once and never saved. Replaces the current connection if there is one. Prefer connect when the user already has a tl_ key.

password.description: Used once to mint an API key; never stored

annotations.title: Sign in to TaskLite with email and password

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Disconnect this machine from TaskLite by forgetting the stored credential. Use before connecting a different account, or to revoke local access. Does not delete anything in TaskLite itself and does not revoke the key server-side.

tools.name: list_organizations
tools.description: List the organizations the authenticated user belongs to. Use the returned id as organizationId in other tools.

tools.name: get_email_usage
tools.description: How much of the monthly email quota an organization has used: emails sent this month, emails waiting in the queue, the plan limit (Free 300, Plus 3000, Pro 20000; null means unlimited), whether the plan allows marketing email, and whether sending is paused for the organization (too many bounces or complaints). Covers email sent by automations, the communications endpoints and app servers (POST /apps/<slug>/api/_email/send).

organizationId.description: Defaults to the credential organization

tools.name: configure_external_access
tools.description: Read or change how EXTERNAL users (people who sign up to your app through TaskLite auth) get into an organization. This policy governs sign-up by email and password and by Google. Sign-in by a phone code (POST /auth/otp/send, then /auth/otp/verify) obeys only "invite": under "closed", "approval" and "open" any phone that verifies a code becomes an external member of the organization, who reaches nothing until an endpoint's row-level security or the app's access list (add_app_user) gives them something; under "invite" a new phone needs an invite code or an add_app_user grant. The two ways in that obey the whole policy: email and password (POST /auth/register-external with this organizationId, then POST /auth/login), or Google (POST /auth/google-external with a Google ID token and this organizationId). Either way the answer carries a token the app sends as Authorization: Bearer on every App API call. registrationPolicy: "open", in at once; "approval", an organization admin approves each signup (TaskLite mails the admins on every signup, and the person once approved; unapproved users are never billed); "invite", a new person gets in only with an invite code (create_app_invite, or a code a user of the app minted on a relation endpoint with allowInvites): the app sends it as inviteCode with POST /auth/otp/verify, /auth/register-external or /auth/google-external, a sign-up without one is refused with 403 INVITE_REQUIRED and a bad code with 403 INVITE_INVALID, while people who are already members keep signing in as before; "closed" (the default), self-signup refused, external users are created by an admin. Under every policy a valid invite code admits its holder as if the organization were open, so "invite" is the policy for an app where people join only through someone who invited them (a coach inviting trainees). appLoginUrl: the page of YOUR app where these users log in, it becomes the "Log in" button in the approval email, so set it whenever you deploy an app that uses this flow; pass "" to clear. Call with no changes to just read the current settings. Requires organization admin.

organizationId.description: Defaults to the credential organization

registrationPolicy.description: How external sign-ups are admitted: open, approval, invite (only with an invite code) or closed

appLoginUrl.description: https URL of your app's login page for external users; "" clears it

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List projects in an organization. The API returns 50 per page, an organization with more than that needs page 2 and beyond, so check the returned total before assuming a project does not exist.

organizationId.description: Defaults to the credential organization

tools.name: list_boards
tools.description: List the boards inside a project, id, name, description. Every other board tool needs a boardId, and this is the only way to discover one without being handed a URL.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project (a business process container). Boards with data live inside projects.

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.name: create_board
tools.description: Create a board (a data table) inside a project. Add typed columns with create_column afterwards. kind: "tasks" (default) also gives the board the built-in task columns, status, priority, assignee, due date, tags, for work people track; "data" creates a plain table with only the columns you add, for records such as customers, products or orders (requires a TaskLite server from 2026-09-06; older servers ignore kind).

kind.description: "tasks": with the built-in task columns (status, priority, assignee, due date, tags). "data": only the columns you add. Default tasks.

tools.name: create_column
tools.description: Add a typed column to a board. Valid types: text, rich_text, number, status, date, datetime, duration, people, checkbox, dropdown, label, priority, link, email, phone, relation, lookup, rollup, formula, rating, currency, file. Choose by meaning, date for dates, phone for phones, number/currency for amounts, dropdown/status (with settings.options as an array of labels) for closed choices; text is for free text only. An obvious name/type mismatch is rejected with the suggested type; pass force:true to override. Rules go in settings.validation: { unique, min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, patternMessage }, enforced on every write (UI, MCP, App API). Closed choices (dropdown/status) reject values outside settings.options unless settings.allowCustom is true.

type.description: Action type: http_request, send_notification, send_email, send_whatsapp, change_status, set_column_value, create_cross_board_item, send_webhook or delay

settings.description: Type-specific settings. For dropdown/status/priority: options, either as labels ["A","B"] or as full objects [{value,label,color}], labels are expanded server-side, and colors are assigned if you do not supply them.

isRequired.description: Require a non-blank value on every App API create

force.description: Create the column even when the name suggests a different type

tools.name: get_board_schema
tools.description: Get a board with its full column schema (ids, names, types, settings). Call this before creating items with cells.

tools.name: update_board
tools.description: Rename a board or change its description. Structure (columns) is changed with update_column / delete_column / reorder_columns.

tools.name: delete_board
tools.description: Delete a board with every item on it. Destructive and not undoable, confirm with the user first, and prefer delete_column when only part of the model is wrong.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Delete a project with every board, column and row inside it. Destructive: confirm with the user first, and name the project in the confirmation. The project goes to the organization recycle bin, so it can be restored from the admin until it is emptied.

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.name: update_column
tools.description: Change a column after the fact: rename it, change its type (e.g. number -> currency), replace settings (dropdown options), or set isRequired / isHidden. A type change converts existing values (number↔currency, text→number/date/checkbox, anything→text) and clears the ones that cannot convert; the response carries conversion: { converted, cleared }. settings.validation rules apply here too.

type.description: New column type (same list as create_column)

settings.description: Replaces the column settings, e.g. { options: [...] } for dropdown/status

isRequired.description: Require a non-blank value on every App API create

isHidden.description: Hide the column in the TaskLite UI

tools.name: delete_column
tools.description: Delete a column and every value stored in it. Destructive, confirm with the user first. Use update_column when the column is right but its name, type or options are wrong.

tools.name: reorder_columns
tools.description: Set the display order of a board's columns. Pass every column id in the wanted order (get_board_schema lists them).

columnIds.description: Column ids in the new order (every column of the board)

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: The whole project as JSON, boards, columns with settings, items with their cells keyed by column id. For migrations, backups and reading a system back. Items are capped per board for the model's sake; the REST endpoint GET /organizations/{orgId}/projects/{projectId}/export.json returns everything.

organizationId.description: Defaults to the credential organization

tools.name: query_items
tools.description: List items (rows) of a board, including their cell values. Returns all items unless limit/page are given (the API defaults to 50 per page when unpaged, so the tool pages through and concatenates). Narrow the result with search, status, priority and sort instead of fetching everything. This is the admin view; the REST endpoints of a published app take a fuller grammar, filter[column][gte], relation filters, per-field search, see get_app_spec.

search.description: Free text; matches the row title and its text cells

status.description: Only rows whose status is one of these, comma separated. Matched against the board's status column by option value or label, case-insensitive: "todo,in_progress" on a task board, "Received,In Repair" on a data board whose status column lists those (get_board_schema shows the options). Needs a status column. A board with none (no column of type status) gets an error that lists its dropdown columns, instead of unfiltered rows. A board whose status is a dropdown named status/סטטוס/מצב is filtered here on that dropdown, after fetching, so an explicit limit can give a page with fewer rows (the answer says so)

excludeStatus.description: Only rows whose status is NOT one of these, comma separated, resolved like status. The way to ask for everything that is not done: excludeStatus "done" (task board) or "Completed" (a data board with that option). Rows with no status at all are kept. A board without a status column is handled as for status: an error, or a filter here on a dropdown named status/סטטוס/מצב

priority.description: Only rows with one of these priorities, comma separated (task boards only)

sort.description: Sort by title, createdAt, updatedAt or status; prefix with "-" for descending, e.g. "-createdAt" for newest first. Anything else keeps the board order

archived.description: Which rows to include. Default active

limit.description: Page size; omit to fetch all items

tools.description: Create an item (row) with all of its data in one call. cells maps columnId -> value (use get_board_schema for column ids); every cell is saved with the row. Use set_cell only for later edits.

title.description: Item title, shown as the row name

status.description: Task status of the row on a task board: todo, in_progress, review or done. Refused on a data board, where it would only write a hidden task field: set that board's status column with cells (create_item) or set_cell (update_item) instead

priority.description: Priority: low, medium, high or urgent

tags.description: Tags as an array of strings

cells.description: Cell values keyed by column id: { "<columnId>": value }. Scalars, { amount, currency } for currency, { relatedItemIds: [...] } for relations

tools.name: update_item
tools.description: Update item fields (title, description, status, priority, dueDate, tags). On a data board the task fields (status, priority, dueDate, tags) are hidden: its columns, status included, are set with set_cell.

title.description: Item title, shown as the row name

status.description: Task status of the row on a task board: todo, in_progress, review or done. Refused on a data board, where it would only write a hidden task field: set that board's status column with cells (create_item) or set_cell (update_item) instead

priority.description: Priority: low, medium, high or urgent

dueDate.description: Due date, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD or full timestamp)

tags.description: Tags as an array of strings

tools.name: set_cell
tools.description: Set a single cell value on an item by columnId.

value.description: The new cell value; shape depends on the column type

tools.name: get_cells
tools.description: Read cells of one item from the database (not a cache): one current value per column, the value set_cells_if_unchanged compares. Use it to decide a conditional write, and pass each value back as `expected` exactly as it came.

columnIds.description: Only these columns (default: every cell of the item)

tools.name: set_cells_if_unchanged
tools.description: Compare-and-set on cells of one item, all or none. Each cell carries the value you read (`expected`, null = empty) and the value to write. If any cell no longer holds its `expected`, nothing is written and the answer is an error with code CELL_CONFLICT and `conflicts` [{columnId, current}]: read again (use `current`), decide again, and never resend the same call. CELL_BUSY (the row is being written) also writes nothing: read again, then retry. Plain columns only (not relation, file, lookup, rollup, formula, button or system columns). Use set_cell for a write that needs no precondition.

value.description: The value to write; null clears the cell

expected.description: The value you read, exactly as it came back (null = empty or missing)

cells.description: 1 to 50 cells of this item, each column once

tools.name: request_file_upload
tools.description: Create a link that puts files onto an item from outside TaskLite: the customer's photos, a signed contract, a logo, a build zip. Returns an address like https://app.tasklite.net/upload/<token> that anyone you hand it to can use with no account, no login and no API key; pass clientEmail and TaskLite emails the link for you. What arrives lands as attachments on that item, and list_uploaded_files reads them back with a download URL. This is the answer when the person has the file and the model does not: a hosted client cannot read a folder on someone's machine. The link is public for as long as it lasts, so keep expiryDays short and maxFiles tight, and revoke_upload_link when the material is in.

itemId.description: Item (row) the files belong to, from query_items / create_item. Make the row first if the material has no home yet

clientName.description: Who is being asked, shown on the upload page

clientEmail.description: Send the link to this address. Omit to get the link back and pass it on yourself

message.description: What to upload, in the words the recipient will read: "the four room photos and the price list"

maxFiles.description: How many files the link accepts before it stops. Default 10

expiryDays.description: How long the link lives. Default 7 days

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.name: list_uploaded_files
tools.description: The files attached to an item, including everything that came in through a request_file_upload link, each with a download URL that is signed and short lived (mint a fresh one by calling again). Also lists the upload links on the item and how many files each has taken, which is how to tell whether the person you asked has delivered.

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.name: create_signature_request
tools.description: Send a PDF for electronic signature and get the signing links back. One call: the PDF (an attachment already on an item, see list_uploaded_files / request_file_upload, or the bytes as base64), the signers, and optionally the row it belongs to. Each signer opens a personal link with an expiry, confirms a one-time code sent to their email or WhatsApp, reads the document and signs; the platform then seals the PDF with an evidence page and emails every signer the signed copy. With no fields, a signature page (name, signature, date per signer) is added at the end, so "read, then sign at the end" needs no coordinates. With itemId and signedFileColumnId (a file column on that item's board), the signed PDF is added to that cell when everyone has signed: build what happens next as an automation on "column value changed" of that column (set a status, notify, webhook). sendEmail=false skips the invitation emails and the links are yours to hand over (WhatsApp, open on the agent's phone). For a customer app the same thing is in its own API: /api/_esign (script /api/_esign/sign, TaskLiteSign).

message.description: A note shown in the invitation and on the signing page

pdfAttachmentId.description: Attachment id of a PDF already uploaded (list_uploaded_files)

pdfBase64.description: Or the PDF itself, base64 (up to 10MB)

email.description: Required: the code (unless WhatsApp) and the signed copy go here

order.description: Signing order; equal orders sign in parallel, later orders are invited when earlier ones finish

x.description: Fraction of page width from the left

y.description: Fraction of page height from the top

fields.description: Where each signer signs. Omit to append a signature page

itemId.description: The row this document belongs to

signedFileColumnId.description: File column on the item's board that receives the signed PDF

expiryDays.description: How long the links work. Default 14

sendEmail.description: Email invitations. Default true; links are returned either way

sendSignedCopy.description: Email every signer the signed copy at the end. Default true

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.name: list_signature_requests
tools.description: Documents sent for signature, newest first, with each signer's state (sent, viewed, signed, declined). Filter by the row they belong to or by status (out_for_signature, completed, declined, voided, expired, failed).

itemId.description: Only documents tied to this row

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.description: One document sent for signature: status, signers and their state, and when complete a short-lived download URL of the signed PDF (with its evidence page).

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

appId.description: App id or slug (from list_apps / create_app)

appId.description: App id or slug (from list_apps / create_app)

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

tools.name: create_app_endpoint
tools.description: Expose a board as a REST endpoint of an app: /apps/{appSlug}/api/{slug}. exposedColumns limits which columns are readable/writable. rowLevelSecurity.enabled makes the endpoint per-user: the developer's server sends `X-App-User: <their user id>` next to the API key, and the endpoint returns, updates and deletes ONLY that user's rows (401 without the header). Use it whenever the app has its own users. rowLevelSecurity.mode chooses which rows a user reaches: owner (the rows they created), shared (all rows, for authorized users), phone (the rows that carry their verified phone) or relation (the rows linked through a relation column to the row that stands for them). An app with two kinds of people in one organization, coaches and their trainees, is built from these: the Coaches board in mode phone (phoneColumn = its phone column), so each coach reads and edits his own row; Trainees in mode relation with relationColumn = its Coach column and identityPhoneColumn = the Coaches phone column, so a coach who signed in by phone sees only his trainees; boards one hop further (weigh-ins of a trainee) in mode relation with relationColumn = the Trainee column and viaColumn = Trainees.Coach for the coach, plus a second endpoint on the same board without viaColumn for the trainee herself. A trainee becomes her row through an invite code (create_app_invite, or allowInvites so the coach mints it in the app) or link_app_user.

appId.description: App id or slug (from list_apps / create_app)

slug.description: URL slug: lowercase letters, digits and dashes

allowedMethods.description: HTTP methods the endpoint accepts: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE

alias.description: JSON key exposed for this column: letters, digits, underscore. Never one of the reserved item fields id, title, description, status, priority, dueDate, assignedTo, createdAt, updatedAt, order, appUserId, a business status column becomes repairStatus or orderStatus, not status.

readOnly.description: Expose the column for reading only; writes to it are refused with 400

exposedColumns.description: Columns the endpoint reads and writes, with the JSON key each one gets; without it the endpoint returns bare metadata

enabled.description: true: every request must carry a signed-in user (the token from sign-in, or the app key with X-App-User)

mode.description: "owner" (default): each user sees and edits only the rows they created. "shared": every user authorized on the app (on its access list, or an owner, admin or editor of the organization) sees and edits every row; the mode for an admin screen or a team system. Anyone else who signs in is refused with 403, so put the people who run the app on the list with add_app_user (their phone and a role; it works before their first sign-in). "phone": a user signed in with a code sent to their phone sees and edits only the rows whose phoneColumn holds that phone, e.g. a directory where each person keeps their own card, or the Coaches board itself in a coaching app (each coach reads and edits his own row; a POST writes his verified phone into the row whatever the body says). "relation": each user reaches the rows whose relationColumn points at the row that stands for them, e.g. a Trainees board whose "Coach" relation column points at the Coaches board: a coach sees only his trainees. A relation endpoint never returns the row that IS the user, only rows pointing at it, so expose the identity board itself through a second endpoint in mode "phone". In relation mode a new row is linked to the caller by the server, the link cannot be moved with PATCH, and a user who stands for no row gets an empty list on GET and 403 on POST. "policy": the endpoint follows the access policy of its board (set_board_policy): business roles (define_app_role and grant_app_role, or set_policy_identity), row scope per role, per-column read and write rules. It takes no other rowLevelSecurity field; the board needs a policy and the users need roles, so test with explain_access and simulate_request

phoneColumn.description: mode "phone" only, required there: the column that holds each row's phone number. A column id (get_board_schema)

emailColumn.description: mode "phone" only, optional, next to phoneColumn: a column that holds each row's email. A user whose email was proved by a login code also reaches the rows that carry that address; for people whose number takes no SMS (outside Israel the code goes by email, which proves the email, not the phone). A column id (get_board_schema)

relationColumn.description: mode "relation" only, required there: a RELATION column on this endpoint's board. A row belongs to the caller when this column points at an item that stands for the caller (or, with viaColumn, at an item that points at one). Example: on the Trainees board, the "Coach" column. A column id (get_board_schema)

viaColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: one more hop. A RELATION column on the board that relationColumn points to, leading to the board of the caller's own items. Example: a Weigh-ins endpoint with relationColumn = Weigh-ins."Trainee" and viaColumn = Trainees."Coach" lets a coach reach the weigh-ins of all his trainees. For the trainee herself, make a second endpoint on the same board with relationColumn = "Trainee" and no viaColumn. A column id (get_board_schema of that other board)

identityPhoneColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: a phone column on the board where the caller's own items live (the board relationColumn points to, or with viaColumn the board viaColumn points to). A user whose VERIFIED phone (sign-in by a code sent to that phone) is written in a row there stands for that row, with no invite and no link. Example: Coaches."Phone", so a coach who signed in by phone is his own Coaches row at once. Whoever may write that column decides who the row is, so expose it readOnly wherever it must not move. A column id (get_board_schema of that board)

identityEmailColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: like identityPhoneColumn, for an email column and a user whose email was verified by a login code. A column id (get_board_schema of that board)

allowInvites.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true lets a user of the app mint an invite code for a row they reach through this endpoint (POST /apps/{appSlug}/api/{endpointSlug}/{itemId}/invites with body { maxUses?, expiresInDays?, label? }; the endpoint must also allow POST). A coach invites a trainee to the trainee's own row; whoever signs up with the code is linked to that row. Such an invite never grants an access role. Without it only an owner or admin creates invites (create_app_invite)

singleLink.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true gives each row of this endpoint's board to ONE linked user. Once someone is linked to a row, another person redeeming an invite code for the same row is refused (the sign-up answers inviteRedeemed: false with inviteError "INVITE_ROW_TAKEN"), so a coach cannot become a trainee's row from a second account. Whoever is already linked is not affected, and the app owner can still link by hand (link_app_user). Set it on the endpoint of the board whose rows are invited to, e.g. Trainees

editOwnOnly.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true lets everyone the relation reaches READ a row, while only the user who created it may PATCH or DELETE it, or change its files (others get 403 with code ROW_NOT_YOURS). For rows two people both see but only one of them owns, e.g. a trainee's own log that her coach reads

rowLevelSecurity.description: Row-level security. Off: whoever holds the app key reads everything. On: every request must name a signed-in user, and mode decides which rows they reach. Only the keys listed here exist; an unknown key is refused, not ignored

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

enabled.description: true: every request must carry a signed-in user (the token from sign-in, or the app key with X-App-User)

mode.description: "owner" (default): each user sees and edits only the rows they created. "shared": every user authorized on the app (on its access list, or an owner, admin or editor of the organization) sees and edits every row; the mode for an admin screen or a team system. Anyone else who signs in is refused with 403, so put the people who run the app on the list with add_app_user (their phone and a role; it works before their first sign-in). "phone": a user signed in with a code sent to their phone sees and edits only the rows whose phoneColumn holds that phone, e.g. a directory where each person keeps their own card, or the Coaches board itself in a coaching app (each coach reads and edits his own row; a POST writes his verified phone into the row whatever the body says). "relation": each user reaches the rows whose relationColumn points at the row that stands for them, e.g. a Trainees board whose "Coach" relation column points at the Coaches board: a coach sees only his trainees. A relation endpoint never returns the row that IS the user, only rows pointing at it, so expose the identity board itself through a second endpoint in mode "phone". In relation mode a new row is linked to the caller by the server, the link cannot be moved with PATCH, and a user who stands for no row gets an empty list on GET and 403 on POST. "policy": the endpoint follows the access policy of its board (set_board_policy): business roles (define_app_role and grant_app_role, or set_policy_identity), row scope per role, per-column read and write rules. It takes no other rowLevelSecurity field; the board needs a policy and the users need roles, so test with explain_access and simulate_request

phoneColumn.description: mode "phone" only, required there: the column that holds each row's phone number. A column id (get_board_schema)

emailColumn.description: mode "phone" only, optional, next to phoneColumn: a column that holds each row's email. A user whose email was proved by a login code also reaches the rows that carry that address; for people whose number takes no SMS (outside Israel the code goes by email, which proves the email, not the phone). A column id (get_board_schema)

relationColumn.description: mode "relation" only, required there: a RELATION column on this endpoint's board. A row belongs to the caller when this column points at an item that stands for the caller (or, with viaColumn, at an item that points at one). Example: on the Trainees board, the "Coach" column. A column id (get_board_schema)

viaColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: one more hop. A RELATION column on the board that relationColumn points to, leading to the board of the caller's own items. Example: a Weigh-ins endpoint with relationColumn = Weigh-ins."Trainee" and viaColumn = Trainees."Coach" lets a coach reach the weigh-ins of all his trainees. For the trainee herself, make a second endpoint on the same board with relationColumn = "Trainee" and no viaColumn. A column id (get_board_schema of that other board)

identityPhoneColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: a phone column on the board where the caller's own items live (the board relationColumn points to, or with viaColumn the board viaColumn points to). A user whose VERIFIED phone (sign-in by a code sent to that phone) is written in a row there stands for that row, with no invite and no link. Example: Coaches."Phone", so a coach who signed in by phone is his own Coaches row at once. Whoever may write that column decides who the row is, so expose it readOnly wherever it must not move. A column id (get_board_schema of that board)

identityEmailColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: like identityPhoneColumn, for an email column and a user whose email was verified by a login code. A column id (get_board_schema of that board)

allowInvites.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true lets a user of the app mint an invite code for a row they reach through this endpoint (POST /apps/{appSlug}/api/{endpointSlug}/{itemId}/invites with body { maxUses?, expiresInDays?, label? }; the endpoint must also allow POST). A coach invites a trainee to the trainee's own row; whoever signs up with the code is linked to that row. Such an invite never grants an access role. Without it only an owner or admin creates invites (create_app_invite)

singleLink.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true gives each row of this endpoint's board to ONE linked user. Once someone is linked to a row, another person redeeming an invite code for the same row is refused (the sign-up answers inviteRedeemed: false with inviteError "INVITE_ROW_TAKEN"), so a coach cannot become a trainee's row from a second account. Whoever is already linked is not affected, and the app owner can still link by hand (link_app_user). Set it on the endpoint of the board whose rows are invited to, e.g. Trainees

editOwnOnly.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true lets everyone the relation reaches READ a row, while only the user who created it may PATCH or DELETE it, or change its files (others get 403 with code ROW_NOT_YOURS). For rows two people both see but only one of them owns, e.g. a trainee's own log that her coach reads

rowLevelSecurity.description: Replacement row-level security (same shape as create_app_endpoint); null turns it off. The object replaces the stored one whole, it is not merged: to change one field, read the current value with list_app_endpoints and send every field again (enabled, mode and the columns of that mode), or the ones left out are lost

tools.description: Delete an endpoint of an app for good: /apps/{appSlug}/api/{slug} stops answering at once and the endpoint cannot be brought back (create it again with create_app_endpoint). The board and its rows are not touched. Confirm with the user first: a frontend that calls this endpoint breaks. To take an endpoint offline and keep its definition, use update_app_endpoint with isActive false instead (list_app_endpoints shows active endpoints only, so keep the id). Get the endpoint id from list_app_endpoints.

tools.name: configure_app_settings
tools.description: Read or change the settings object of an app. Call with only appId to read. To change, pass set: the keys in it are MERGED into the current settings (objects merge key by key at every depth, arrays and plain values replace, null removes a key). The server itself does not merge: PATCH replaces the whole settings object with what it is sent, so this tool reads the app, merges, and writes the full object back; two writers at the same moment can still overwrite each other, so do not run it in parallel on one app. Settings the server reads: ai (AI actions the app may run: { enabled: true, userDaily?, appDaily?, actions: { "<name>": { instructions, output?: "text"|"json", schema? (a JSON Schema, required for json), inputs?: { "<input>": { maxChars?, required? } }, tier?: "fast"|"smart", maxOutputTokens?, temperature?, audience?: "users"|"server" } } }. The instructions stay on the server: a page runs an action by name with POST /apps/<slug>/api/_ai/v1/run { action, input } and the signed-in user's own token (the app's server may use a key with the "ai" scope). Every run is charged to the owner's usage allowance; 429 AI_QUOTA_EXCEEDED, AI_USER_DAILY_LIMIT or AI_RATE_LIMIT carry messageHe/message to show. An app without sign-in cannot run AI actions), passwordReset.returnUrls (array of up to 50 URLs the "reset password" email may send a user back to, matched by scheme, host, port and path prefix; needed only for a custom app scheme such as myapp://reset or a domain other than the app's own {slug}.tasklite.dev and its connected custom domains, which are always allowed; http is never accepted), language (the language of the password reset email: a value starting with "he" gives Hebrew, any other value English; left out, the user's own language decides), endUserDeletion.rows ("delete": when an end user deletes their account, the rows they wrote in this app are deleted with it and erased for good 30 days later; left out, the rows stay with the author shown as a deleted account). Other keys are stored as given and returned, and the server does not act on them.

tools.name: list_app_users
tools.description: List the people of an app, as { users, pending }. users: everyone who ever called it with X-App-User or signed in to it with a code. Each has userId (the id set_app_user_role, remove_app_user, link_app_user, list_app_user_links and send_test_push take), externalId (the developer's own id for them, or null for a user who signed in by code), name, phone (the phone they proved with a code, or null), source (api or otp), role (viewer, editor or submitter), isActive, hasAccessRow, lastSeenAt and itemCount (rows they own on the app's boards). hasAccessRow says whether they are on the app's access list: when it is false, role and isActive are only defaults, and an endpoint in row-level security mode "shared" refuses them with 403 until add_app_user or set_app_user_role puts them on the list. pending: the phones add_app_user is still holding access for, each with id, phone, role, createdAt, expiresAt and status (pending, or expired); they get in on their first sign-in with a code. Use it to see who can use the app and to find the userId of a person.

tools.name: add_app_user
tools.description: Give a person access to an app by their phone number: the phone and a role, nothing else. This is how the people who run an app (the business owner, a manager, staff) get into its admin screen, whose endpoints are in row-level security mode "shared". The person needs no invite code and does not have to sign in first. If the phone already signed in to this organization with a code, access is on at once and the answer has status "active" and their userId. Otherwise the answer has status "pending" and a pendingId: nothing is created for the number yet, and the access opens by itself the first time that phone signs in to the app with an SMS code (POST /auth/otp/send, then /auth/otp/verify). The phone is matched whatever its spelling: 054-1234567, +972 54 123 4567 and 972541234567 are one number; a number outside Israel needs its country code. Calling again for the same phone sets its role again, and switches back on a user who was switched off. Roles: editor (reads and writes), viewer (reads), submitter (creates). The app must still sign people in by phone code; a person who signs in another way (email and password, Google) is a different account, give them access with set_app_user_role after their first sign-in. Requires organization owner or admin (an editor gets 403).

tools.name: create_app_invite
tools.description: Create an invite code for an app (8 characters shown as XXXX-XXXX, typed without regard to case or the dash). The person signs up or signs in through the app with the code: the app sends it as inviteCode with POST /auth/otp/verify, /auth/register-external or /auth/google-external, after it may check it with POST /auth/invites/check. An invite does one or both of two things, and must do at least one: itemId links the new user to that row, so they "are" the row for every endpoint in row-level security mode "relation" (invite a trainee to her own Trainees row, or a coach to his Coaches row); role puts them on the app's access list (viewer, editor or submitter), which is what mode "shared" endpoints check. A valid code also admits a new person into an organization whose registration policy is "invite" or "closed" (configure_external_access). An existing access row is never changed by an invite: it does not re-enable a user who was switched off and does not raise a role. Requires organization owner or admin (an editor gets 403). To let the app's own users invite (a coach invites his trainees from inside the app), set allowInvites on the relation endpoint instead; the app then calls POST /apps/{appSlug}/api/{endpointSlug}/{itemId}/invites.

tools.name: set_board_policy
tools.description:
Set who may read, write, create and delete rows of a board, and which columns, as a JSON document (a FULL REPLACE of the board's policy; read get_board_policy first to change part of one). It is enforced on the app's endpoints of this board whose rowLevelSecurity.mode is "policy" (create_app_endpoint / update_app_endpoint). Organization owners, admins and editors using the app are let through unless internalBypass is false. Fields:
- schemaVersion: 1 (required).
- internalBypass: default true.
- rows.read / rows.write: a list of { roles, scope }. scope is "all", { "mine": "<column id>" } (rows whose column points at the caller: a relation to the row that stands for them, their verified phone or email, or a people column; add "via": "<relation column id>" for one more hop), { "created": true } (rows they created through the app) or { "where": CONDITION } (rows a condition selects, e.g. open cases older than 3 days, for an escalation view). A user gets the union of the rules that name any of their roles; no rule for their roles means no access.
- rows.create / rows.delete: plain role lists.
- columns: { "<column id or reserved field>": { "read": ACCESS, "write": ACCESS } }. ACCESS is a role list, or { "roles": [...], "orMine": "<column id>" } (these roles, or anyone for whom the row is theirs by that column). A column without an entry follows the row rules. An EMPTY list ("write": []) locks the column for everyone through the app: use it for assignedTo and for any field only an admin or an action may change. Reserved fields are title, description, status, priority, dueDate and assignedTo, addressed by those names. Reserved fields are open to anyone who may write the row unless you lock them, so lock assignedTo.
- CONDITION (in where, rules.when): { "all": [c...] } | { "any": [c...] } | { "not": c } | a leaf { "col": "<column id or reserved field>", "op": OP, ... }. OP: eq / neq (with "value"), in (value is a list), empty, notEmpty, isMe (the column points at the caller; optional "via"), olderThan (col is updatedAt, createdAt or a date column; give "hours" or "days"), changed (this write sets col; only in rules). No free expressions.
- rules: [{ "id", "when": CONDITION, "deny": { "write": "*" | [column ids], "except": [roles] }, "require": [column ids that must be filled after the write], "except": [roles], "message" }]. deny is judged on the row as it is BEFORE the write, require AFTER it. Rules bind people acting through the app; internal bypass users and an action's own columns are not held to deny.
- actions: { "<name>": { "roles": [...], "input": { "<input name>": { "col": "<column id the value is written to>", "required": true } }, "set": { "<column id>": constant }, "event": "TRANSFER", "scope": "write" | "read", "approval": "<approval workflow id of the board>" } }. An action is role-gated, validates its input (an input without col is only data; "reason" is always accepted and goes to the history), writes its set and bound inputs in one transaction, and records event and reason in the history. It is the only way to change a column whose write is []. With approval it files a request for that workflow instead of writing; the write happens when the last step approves. Roles named by approval steps must exist (define_app_role). Actions run through the App API only (see below).
Frontends run an action with POST /apps/<slug>/api/<endpoint>/<itemId>/actions/<name> and the inputs as the body; approvers read GET /apps/<slug>/api/me/approvals and answer POST /apps/<slug>/api/approvals/<requestId>/decide { "decision": "approve" | "reject", "comment"? }; GET /apps/<slug>/api/me/permissions lists the actions the caller may run as [{ name, allowed, roles, inputs, approval, event, scope }]. There is no MCP tool that runs an action.
Roles are keys from list_app_roles, plus "*" (any signed-in user) and "public". Column ids come from get_board_schema. An invalid document is refused with POLICY_INVALID and an errors list naming each problem. Example (agents see and edit only their own cases, the manager sees and edits all, bookkeeping reads all, commission is visible to the owner, the manager and to the agent on his own rows):
{ "schemaVersion": 1,
  "rows": {
    "read":  [ { "roles": ["owner","manager","bookkeeping"], "scope": "all" },
               { "roles": ["agent"], "scope": { "mine": "<agent column id>" } } ],
    "write": [ { "roles": ["owner","manager"], "scope": "all" },
               { "roles": ["agent"], "scope": { "mine": "<agent column id>" } } ],
    "create": ["owner","manager","agent"],
    "delete": ["owner"] },
  "columns": {
    "<commission column id>": { "read": { "roles": ["owner","manager"], "orMine": "<agent column id>" }, "write": ["owner"] },
    "<agent column id>": { "write": ["owner","manager"] },
    "assignedTo": { "write": [] } },
  "rules": [ { "id": "lock", "when": { "all": [ { "col": "<locked column id>", "op": "eq", "value": true } ] },
               "deny": { "write": "*", "except": ["owner","manager"] }, "message": "The case is locked to its agent" } ],
  "actions": {
    "transfer": { "roles": ["owner","manager"], "input": { "agent": { "col": "<agent column id>", "required": true }, "reason": { "required": true } },
                  "set": { "<locked column id>": false }, "event": "TRANSFER" },
    "unlock":   { "roles": ["owner","manager"], "input": { "reason": { "required": true } }, "set": { "<locked column id>": false }, "event": "UNLOCK" },
    "exception": { "roles": ["agent"], "input": { "reason": { "required": true } }, "set": { "<exception column id>": true }, "approval": "<workflow id, a role step>" } } }
(The Achituv shape: a locked case cannot be edited except by the owner and the manager; transfer and unlock are the only way to change the agent or the lock, with a recorded reason; an exception asks a role step for approval.) Test it with explain_access and simulate_request before telling the user it is done. Requires organization owner or admin.

tools.name: build_backend
tools.description: Build a whole backend in one call from a spec you compose: the project, its boards, their typed columns (including relations between the boards), optional sample rows, and optionally a published REST API with one endpoint per board and a server-side key. Use it whenever the user describes a system ("a backend for my repair shop: customers, orders, payments") instead of calling create_project, create_board, create_column, create_app, publish_app, create_app_endpoint and create_app_api_key one by one. You do the design, pick column types by meaning (phone, date, currency, dropdown/status with options for closed choices), link boards with a relation column (type "relation", relatedBoard: "<board name in this spec>", relationType: many_to_one for an order→customer link), and this tool executes it and returns one compact summary. API field names are derived from column names and never collide with reserved item fields, so there is nothing to retry. Boards are created as plain data tables (kind "data": only the columns you define, no task fields); set kind "tasks" on a board where people track work to do and want status, priority, assignee and due date built in. Every row still has a title. When the API has its own users, api.rowLevelSecurity: true gives every endpoint mode "owner"; a board may carry its own rowLevelSecurity instead (mode shared, phone or relation, with columns named as in this spec), e.g. Coaches { mode: "phone", phoneColumn: "Phone" } and Trainees { mode: "relation", relationColumn: "Coach", identityPhoneColumn: "Phone", allowInvites: true }.

Defaults to many_to_many, which is rarely what a business model means, say it.

alias.description: API field name to use instead of the derived one (letters, digits, underscore; not a reserved item field)

enabled.description: Defaults to true; false leaves this endpoint without row-level security

mode.description: "owner" (default): each user sees and edits only the rows they created. "shared": every user authorized on the app (on its access list, or an owner, admin or editor of the organization) sees and edits every row; the mode for an admin screen or a team system. Anyone else who signs in is refused with 403, so put the people who run the app on the list with add_app_user (their phone and a role; it works before their first sign-in). "phone": a user signed in with a code sent to their phone sees and edits only the rows whose phoneColumn holds that phone, e.g. a directory where each person keeps their own card, or the Coaches board itself in a coaching app (each coach reads and edits his own row; a POST writes his verified phone into the row whatever the body says). "relation": each user reaches the rows whose relationColumn points at the row that stands for them, e.g. a Trainees board whose "Coach" relation column points at the Coaches board: a coach sees only his trainees. A relation endpoint never returns the row that IS the user, only rows pointing at it, so expose the identity board itself through a second endpoint in mode "phone". In relation mode a new row is linked to the caller by the server, the link cannot be moved with PATCH, and a user who stands for no row gets an empty list on GET and 403 on POST. "policy": the endpoint follows the access policy of its board (set_board_policy): business roles (define_app_role and grant_app_role, or set_policy_identity), row scope per role, per-column read and write rules. It takes no other rowLevelSecurity field; the board needs a policy and the users need roles, so test with explain_access and simulate_request

emailColumn.description: mode "phone" only, optional, next to phoneColumn: a column that holds each row's email. A user whose email was proved by a login code also reaches the rows that carry that address; for people whose number takes no SMS (outside Israel the code goes by email, which proves the email, not the phone). The NAME of a column of this board in the spec

relationColumn.description: mode "relation" only, required there: a RELATION column on this endpoint's board. A row belongs to the caller when this column points at an item that stands for the caller (or, with viaColumn, at an item that points at one). Example: on the Trainees board, the "Coach" column. The NAME of a relation column of this board in the spec

viaColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: one more hop. A RELATION column on the board that relationColumn points to, leading to the board of the caller's own items. Example: a Weigh-ins endpoint with relationColumn = Weigh-ins."Trainee" and viaColumn = Trainees."Coach" lets a coach reach the weigh-ins of all his trainees. For the trainee herself, make a second endpoint on the same board with relationColumn = "Trainee" and no viaColumn. The NAME of a relation column of the board relationColumn points to

identityPhoneColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: a phone column on the board where the caller's own items live (the board relationColumn points to, or with viaColumn the board viaColumn points to). A user whose VERIFIED phone (sign-in by a code sent to that phone) is written in a row there stands for that row, with no invite and no link. Example: Coaches."Phone", so a coach who signed in by phone is his own Coaches row at once. Whoever may write that column decides who the row is, so expose it readOnly wherever it must not move. The NAME of a column of that board in the spec

identityEmailColumn.description: mode "relation" only, optional: like identityPhoneColumn, for an email column and a user whose email was verified by a login code. The NAME of a column of that board in the spec

allowInvites.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true lets a user of the app mint an invite code for a row they reach through this endpoint (POST /apps/{appSlug}/api/{endpointSlug}/{itemId}/invites with body { maxUses?, expiresInDays?, label? }; the endpoint must also allow POST). A coach invites a trainee to the trainee's own row; whoever signs up with the code is linked to that row. Such an invite never grants an access role. Without it only an owner or admin creates invites (create_app_invite)

singleLink.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true gives each row of this endpoint's board to ONE linked user. Once someone is linked to a row, another person redeeming an invite code for the same row is refused (the sign-up answers inviteRedeemed: false with inviteError "INVITE_ROW_TAKEN"), so a coach cannot become a trainee's row from a second account. Whoever is already linked is not affected, and the app owner can still link by hand (link_app_user). Set it on the endpoint of the board whose rows are invited to, e.g. Trainees

editOwnOnly.description: mode "relation" only, default false: true lets everyone the relation reaches READ a row, while only the user who created it may PATCH or DELETE it, or change its files (others get 403 with code ROW_NOT_YOURS). For rows two people both see but only one of them owns, e.g. a trainee's own log that her coach reads

Columns are given by NAME as written in this spec (the ids do not exist yet). Only the keys listed here exist; an unknown key is refused, not ignored

"title" sets the row title; without it the first plain text value is used, and failing that the row is named after its board and position. A row that other boards reference must carry a title (or a text value) so the reference can be resolved. A relation cell takes the title(s) of rows in the related board (any order in the spec; rows are created in dependency order).

For shared, phone or relation modes set rowLevelSecurity on the board itself

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create an automation on a board: when something happens, do something. The most useful action here is http_request, which calls an external API and writes the answer back into columns, pair it with the "scheduled" trigger and the board keeps itself up to date (prices, exchange rates, shipment status, weather). Triggers: item_created, status_changed, column_value_changed, date_approaching, scheduled. Actions: http_request, send_notification, send_email, send_push, change_status, set_column_value, create_cross_board_item, send_webhook. The scheduled trigger has no cron expression: the server checks once an hour, and triggerConfig takes { intervalHours, runAtHour } only (intervalHours: at least this many hours between runs, default 24; runAtHour: 0-23, run only during that hour of the day in UTC, not in the user's time zone, so convert: 08:00 in Israel is runAtHour 5 in summer and 6 in winter). A scheduled run executes the actions once for every row of the board that passes conditions, so filter with conditions. send_push sends a notification to the phones of app users through the app's own Firebase project (set up once per app: push_status; try it with send_test_push). Its config: { title, body, data, userIds, recipientsFromRelation, includeRowOwner, sound, badge, dataOnly }. title and body take {{column name}} placeholders, title defaults to the row title. Recipients are the union of: the row's owner under row-level security (includeRowOwner, default true; false leaves them out), userIds (fixed user ids, as in list_app_users), and recipientsFromRelation, a dotted path of column NAMES such as "Client.Coach.Coach user" that walks relation columns from this row and whose LAST segment must be a people column holding user ids (a single segment is a people column on this board); it does not resolve the user linked to a row by an invite or by phone, so without such a people column use userIds or the row owner. data is a flat object of strings the app reads to decide where to open (itemId and boardId are added). sound: "default" or the file name of a sound bundled in the app; badge: 0 to 99999, 0 clears; dataOnly: true shows nothing and delivers only data (no title, body, sound or badge; iOS may throttle or drop it). With no recipient the action is skipped, not failed. Two more things every action list can use: a { type: "delay", config: { minutes | hours | days } } action pauses the run and resumes the actions after it later (reminders, follow-ups); and any network action (http_request, send_webhook, send_email, send_whatsapp) may carry config.retry: { attempts (1-5), delaySeconds (1-60) }. send_webhook accepts config.secret for an HMAC signature. send_email sends mail from the organization to the people on a row. Its config: { to, subject, body, columnEmailField, fromName, replyTo, kind, attachments }. kind is "transactional" (the default: orders, receipts, notifications) or "marketing" (promotional mail: it needs the Pro plan or higher and a verified sender domain, and it gets an unsubscribe footer; people who unsubscribed are skipped). attachments is an array of FILE column ids on the triggering row (or {{column.<id>}}): the stored files in those cells are attached, up to 5MB in total, and a missing file is skipped instead of failing the action. Email is counted per month by plan: Free 300, Plus 3000, Pro 20000 (read the numbers with get_email_usage); a message held back by the quota is recorded as skipped in the communications log and can be resent from there. To send email from an app's own server instead of an automation, POST /apps/<slug>/api/_email/send with the app server key (X-API-Key, never a user token; the key needs the "email" or "write" scope, see create_app_api_key): { to: [up to 50 addresses], subject, html or text, replyTo, kind, attachmentIds: [stored file ids] }; each app may send 500 a day (429 APP_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT). create_cross_board_item copies a new row to another board: config { targetBoardId, title?: "{{item.title}}", columnValues: { "<column id on the TARGET board>": "{{<column NAME on this board>}}" } }; there is no mapping field, and a column left out is not copied. To act only on some rows pass conditions, e.g. [{ field: "<column id on this board>", operator: "equals", value: "New seller" }]. Change an automation later with update_automation; call list_automations first so you do not add a second one that does the same thing.

triggerConfig.description: For scheduled: { intervalHours?: number (default 24), runAtHour?: 0-23 in UTC }, e.g. { intervalHours: 1 } for every hour, or { runAtHour: 5, intervalHours: 23 } for once a day at 05:00 UTC. The interval is measured from the previous run, which ends a little after the hour, so with runAtHour use 23, not 24: with 24 the next day's check falls just short and the run slips a day. A cron field is not read. For column_value_changed: { columnName }

tools.name: get_deployment_files
tools.description: Read back what a hosted frontend version is made of: every file with its size and its URL on that version, and the full text of the text files (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, SVG...). This is how a new conversation continues a site an earlier one built: "take my Krispool site and keep going" starts here, not from scratch. For a site written by hand the files ARE the source. For a bundled build (Vite, React) the JS is minified output: fine to inspect, not something to edit, so ask for the project's source instead. Images and other binaries come back as URLs only. Text is capped at 512KB per file and 4MB per call; narrow with `paths` for a big site. To start another app from this version, or bring an old version back as a new one, use deploy_frontend with fromAppId.

appId.description: App id or slug (from list_apps / create_app)

version.description: Version to read (from list_deployments). Default: the live version

paths.description: Only these files, as listed by a previous call, e.g. ["index.html", "css/site.css"]

includeContent.description: false lists the files without their text, a cheap first look at a large site. Default true

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

instructions:
TaskLite is the backend: data lives in boards (tables) inside projects
(one project = one business process). The boards are also the ready-made
admin the end client operates, so you are building a real system.

Connect first: call connection_status. If not connected, this is a new user:
ask for email, name, and a business name, then call sign_up (creates account +
org from here; a password is set locally and never shown). (sign_up exists only
on the local install; hosted connections authenticate via OAuth.)

Finding your way around an existing account: list_projects then list_boards. Changing a model after the fact: update_column (name, type, options), delete_column, reorder_columns, update_board, delete_board, no need to rebuild. create_item saves the title and all cells in one call. Column rules (settings.validation: unique, min/max, pattern) and closed-choice options are enforced on every write, so a 400 names the column and the rule. Automations can pause with a delay action and retry network actions (config.retry). export_project returns the project as JSON. To find something by text across the whole organization: search, then fetch the id it returns.
Both page at 50, so read the total before concluding something is missing.

Build order: create_project -> create_board -> create_column per field, then
get_board_schema to read the real column ids before adding data with create_item
(cells are keyed by those ids). Pick honest types: a status field is a dropdown
with real options, not free text.

Column types carry the whole UX, so choose by meaning and never default to text:
date/datetime for dates and deadlines (unlocks calendar and timeline views),
phone for phone numbers (tap-to-call), email for emails, number or currency for
quantities/prices/amounts, rating for scores, dropdown or status WITH
settings.options for any closed choice, file for uploads. A date stored as text
can never power a calendar, a reminder, or an overdue filter. Long free text or
notes are the only good use of text/rich_text. create_column rejects an obvious
mismatch (e.g. an "Install Date" column typed text) with the suggested type;
retry with that type, or pass force:true if the name is misleading.

Infer a sound schema from the domain instead of asking the user to design tables:
orders/service -> an Orders board (customer, phone, item, status select, price,
due date); CRM -> Contacts + Deals (stage select, value, contact link); bookings
-> one date-keyed board with a status select; inventory -> items (name, sku,
quantity, category select). Prefer few well-typed boards over many thin ones.

When a board needs a number from outside (a price, an exchange rate, a shipment
status, weather) use create_automation with the http_request action:
it calls the API and writes the answer straight into columns via
responseMapping [{ path, columnId }] (ids from get_board_schema). With the
"scheduled" trigger the board refreshes itself, so do not tell the user they
need Make or n8n for this. https only; internal hosts are refused. The
scheduled trigger takes { intervalHours, runAtHour } (runAtHour is in UTC),
not a cron expression. send_push is the action that reaches an app user's
phone.

Only if the user wants an external frontend/app: create_app (needs projectId) ->
create_app_endpoint (choose exposedColumns; enable rowLevelSecurity whenever
the app has its own users) -> publish_app -> create_app_api_key, then
get_frontend_prompt(tool: "claude-code"). The app API key (tk_...) is
server-side only: keep it in an env var and call the app API from server code,
never the browser. exposedColumns is effectively required: an endpoint without
it answers reads with bare item metadata and refuses writes. The app API is
served ONLY from api.tasklite.net; app.tasklite.net is the admin UI and
answers unknown paths with a page, so use the absolute baseUrl from
get_app_spec verbatim. Full reference, including how to read each failure:
https://tasklite.net/docs Users are the developer's own (any sign-in); their server
sends X-App-User: <user id> with the key, and endpoints with rowLevelSecurity
return, update and delete only that user's rows. No user system to build.

rowLevelSecurity.mode picks which rows a user reaches: owner (the rows they
created, the default), shared (all rows, for authorized users), phone (rows
carrying their verified phone), relation (rows linked through a relation
column to the row that stands for them). An app with two kinds of people,
coaches and their trainees: Coaches in mode phone; Trainees in mode relation
with relationColumn = its Coach column and identityPhoneColumn = the Coaches
phone column; a board one hop further (weigh-ins) adds viaColumn. A user "is"
a row by an invite code (create_app_invite, or allowInvites on the endpoint so
a coach invites from inside the app), by link_app_user (ids from
list_app_users), or by a verified phone or email written in the row.
rowLevelSecurity is replaced whole on update and takes only the listed keys.

AI inside an app (summarize, classify, extract fields, draft text): define
named actions in the app's settings with configure_app_settings, set
{ ai: { enabled: true, actions: { "<name>": { instructions, inputs, output } } } },
and call POST /apps/<slug>/api/_ai/v1/run { action, input } with the signed-in
user's token. The model and its key are TaskLite's: never put a model API key
in an app and never call a model provider from a page. Output "json" with a
schema returns parsed data. Runs are charged to the owner's usage allowance;
show the error's messageHe/message on 429. An app without sign-in cannot run
AI actions.

An admin screen (the owner and staff manage the data behind a login): put its
endpoints in mode shared, sign people in by phone code, and call the API at
https://api.tasklite.net with Authorization: Bearer <the token from
/auth/otp/verify>. Then give each person who runs the app access with
add_app_user (their phone and a role). It works before their first sign-in:
the access opens by itself when that phone verifies its first code. Without
it a signed-in person gets 403 on every shared endpoint. Never build a
workaround in the page (a phones board the page syncs from, an invite code
typed by the owner). list_app_users shows who is on the list (hasAccessRow)
and who is still waiting; set_app_user_role changes a role or switches a
user off; remove_app_user takes access away.
Roles and permissions: when different people of one app must see different
rows or columns (a manager all cases, an agent only his own, bookkeeping the
money columns), give the endpoints rowLevelSecurity mode "policy" and the board
a policy. Roles: define_app_role, grant_app_role (userId from list_app_users),
revoke_app_role, or set_policy_identity to read them from an employees board.
Policy: set_board_policy replaces the whole document (get_board_policy first
to change part of it): rows.read/write [{roles, scope: "all" | {mine: columnId}
| {created: true}}], rows.create/delete role lists, columns {columnIdOrReserved
Field: {read, write}} where a list [] locks the column and
{roles, orMine: columnId} means "or his own rows". Always lock assignedTo with
{"write": []}. Then prove it with explain_access and simulate_request.
Beyond roles and columns: scope {where: condition}, write rules (lock a row
unless the role is exempt) and named actions (transfer, unlock: role-gated,
validated input, a fixed set of writes, recorded with an event and a reason;
the only way to change a column locked with []; optional approval workflow).
Actions are App API only: the frontend calls POST /apps/<slug>/api/<endpoint>/
<itemId>/actions/<name>, approvers use GET .../me/approvals and POST
.../approvals/<requestId>/decide. There is no tool that runs one; simulate_request
with action + itemId checks it. get_item_history reads who changed which field of a row.
App-level settings (password reset return URLs, account deletion):
configure_app_settings. Removing an endpoint: delete_app_endpoint.

TaskLite also HOSTS static frontends. deploy_frontend takes the site in one
of three ways: files (inline path+content, from ChatGPT or any hosted client,
write index.html and its assets and deploy in the same turn), zipUrl (a public
https zip such as a Lovable/Bolt export or a GitHub release asset), or dir (a
local build folder, only when the MCP runs next to the files). The result is a
live https://{slug}.tasklite.dev URL, no server or hosting setup on the user's
side. Hosted frontends call the app API at the relative path /api/{endpoint}
(the hosting proxy injects the app identity), so generated code needs no
baseUrl and no tk_ key in the browser. Prefer this flow over telling the user
to host elsewhere; rollback_deployment restores a previous version.

Every item has a comment thread (its correspondence): list_comments to read it,
add_comment to post, passing mentionedUserIds to notify people. Needs projectId +
itemId (get itemId from query_items).

When the app's users should be TaskLite external users instead (the app
signs them up through POST /auth/register-external with the organizationId
and logs them in through POST /auth/login), the organization decides who gets
in: configure_external_access sets the registration policy ("open", in at
once; "approval", an admin approves each one, and TaskLite mails the org's
admins on every signup; "invite", only with an invite code from
create_app_invite, sent as inviteCode with the sign-up call; "closed",
self-signup refused) and appLoginUrl, the page of
YOUR app where those users log in. Set appLoginUrl whenever you deploy such an
app: it is the "Log in" button in the approval email, and without it the
approved user is told nothing about where to go. Unapproved users are never
billed.

Confirm before delete_item. Creation tools return an adminUrl, so end by telling
the user where their ready-made admin is. Pass organizationId explicitly when the
user has more than one org.
